description: This pie chart visually represents the distribution of categories within a dataset, likely for evaluating attribution by large language models as referenced in the paper. The chart is divided into ten distinct slices, each corresponding to a specific category and labeled with its percentage value. The largest segment, colored dark blue, represents “AI/NLP Research” at 24.3%. The second largest segment, a teal-green color, is “Econ. & Fin.” at 18.4%. Other significant segments include “History” (8.2%, olive green), “Science” (6.7%, dark teal), “Law” (5.1%, reddish-brown), “Med & Health” (6.7%, olive green), “Pet & Animal” (5.5%, brown), “Daily Life” (7.1%, teal), “Business” (5.9%, reddish-brown), “Game&Anime” (8.2%, orange), and “Math” (1.2%, dark green). The chart includes a legend-like structure where each category label is connected by a line to its corresponding slice, and all percentage values are explicitly labeled next to their respective category names. The segments appear to be arranged in a clockwise order, generally from largest to smallest, though not perfectly sorted. There are no exploded or emphasized slices, and the chart does not include a traditional legend box.
